facts.text: MuJoCoMessageHandler derives from rclcpp::Node named MuJoCoMessageHandler and sets name_prefix to the relative prefix simulation/.
The node creates the relative sim_reset service with the communication/srv/SimulationReset type.
The node creates the relative actuators_cmds subscription with the communication/msg/ActuatorCmds type and a KeepLast(1) sensor-data QoS.
The node creates the relative joint_states publisher with the sensor_msgs/msg/JointState type.
The reset callback rejects a request whose header.frame_id is not the model name m->names[0] and sets is_success false.

The reset callback calls mj_resetData, writes qpos[0..2] and qpos[3..6] from base_pose.position and base_pose.orientation, writes each named joint's qpos entry and zeroes the cached kp, pos, kd, vel and torque entries.
The reset callback performs those writes between sim_->mtx.lock() and unlock(), then sets is_success true; it does not change sim.run.
While no model data exists the reset callback sleeps in one-second steps as long as rclcpp::ok() holds before it answers.
PhysicsLoop locks the simulation mutex and, while sim.run is set, calls apply_ctrl and mj_step; while paused it only runs mj_forward.
The node starts wall timers for imu_callback every 2.5 ms, joint_callback every 1 ms, odom_callback every 20 ms, touch_callback every 2 ms, img_callback every 20 ms and drop_old_message every 100 ms.
The actuator callback stores the message time, resizes the cached arrays to the message sizes and copies each actuator name, kp, pos, kd, vel and torque entry.
apply_ctrl computes data.ctrl as kp*(pos - jointpos sensordata) + kd*(vel - jointvel sensordata) + torque and clamps the resulting value to the interval [-100, 100].
The stale-command timer zeroes kp, pos, vel and torque and sets kd to 1.0 when the last command time is more than 0.2 s older than the node clock.
joint_callback publishes one JointState entry per hinge joint: its name, qpos position, qvel velocity and qfrc_actuator effort.
img_callback builds a depth-image header and a CvImage from an empty cv::Mat and publishes nothing.
The simulation launch starts the mujoco package's simulation executable with the model-file parameter set to description/model/xml/spot_mini/spot_mini.xml.
The README lists the /simulation/actuators_cmds, /simulation/imu_data, /simulation/joint_states and /simulation/odom topics.
The MJCF is named spot and the base body's initial position is 0 0 0.7.
The MJCF declares 12 hinge joints in four legs, each with a range; for example fl.hx spans -0.785398 to 0.785398 rad, fl.hy spans -0.898845 to 2.29511 rad and fl.kn spans -2.7929 to -0.254402 rad.
The MJCF declares 12 motor actuators named after the 12 hinge joints with gear 1 and no ctrlrange.
The MJCF option element sets timestep to 0.0005 s.

determinism.notes: Event-driven fake with no physics step, PD law, contact or pacing; placeholder arrays do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic rosbridge contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic and not the upstream simulation executable; it runs no MuJoCo physics, PD law, contact, actuator dynamics, sensor or wall-clock loop
the joint-state arrays are 12 placeholder hinge entries; the live node publishes one entry per hinge joint from a 1 ms timer, and the fake does not reproduce that rate

the actuator publication is recorded as a wire message; the fake computes no data.ctrl, applies no real PD law, contact or integration, and only nudges its placeholder joint-position sample by a fixed small factor of the PD expression so a command has an observable contract effect

the resource snapshot subscribes to /simulation/joint_states for each read; the live node publishes it from a 1 ms timer with the model's current qpos, while the fake returns its last placeholder sample
the reset response is modelled; the fake only overwrites placeholder base-pose and joint arrays and clears recorded commands, with no mj_resetData, contact, warm-start or integration state
the 0.0005 s timestep, the 0.2 s stale-command zeroing and the 1 ms/20 ms timers are source facts; the fake has no physics timestep, watchdog or timer behaviour
the depth_image and rgb_image publishers are declared upstream but their callback publishes neither; images, IMU, odometry and touch are NOT COVERED by this package
the reset callback only resets data and cached commands; it does not pause the MuJoCo physics loop, so the simulated bodies continue to step and can fall after the reset

every e-stop calls /simulation/sim_reset twice (the estop binding, then the input-free safe-state action; reviewer probe) and the safety reset binding calls it again; each call teleports the robot back to the start pose; the callback waits in one-second sleeps while no model is loaded, and an unanswered reset makes the e-stop report SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED after its 1 s budget with the latch held (reviewer probe)

kp, pos, kd and vel carry no Limit: the only bound the clone states is the [-100, 100] clamp of the summed control (main.cc:284-285), which the torque Limit applies to the feed-forward term alone; the motors themselves declare no ctrlrange
no live ROS 2 graph, rosbridge endpoint, MuJoCo run or hardware was contacted; the fake is contract_checked evidence only

safe_state.description: Simulated reset, acknowledged after the writes: /simulation/sim_reset calls mj_resetData, puts the base at (0, 0, 0.7) with the model-default hinge positions and zero velocities, and zeroes every cached actuator command, so apply_ctrl writes zero control (joint damping kd 1.0 once the 0.2 s stale timer fires). Physics keeps running unless paused in the GUI: the limp robot falls and settles on the floor. A later actuators_cmds message from any client re-commands it. Not a physical emergency stop.
